title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page: S = T is a trait (spectrum of a DVR) with fraction field K. U/S is an 'elementary' relative scheme, a tower of elementary fibrations in the sense of Artin's bons voisinages, whose 1-dimensional fibres are hyperbolic. A universal cover gives a closure K̄ and the fundamental extensions 1→π→E_{U_K}→E_K→1 and E_U→E_S. Here E_K = Gal(K̄/K), and E_S = π_1(S) is E_K modulo the closed normal subgroup generated by an inertia group I_{x'} ≅ T_∞(K̄) = lim μ_n (prime-to-p part).

A K-rational point f_K of U_K gives a section ψ: E_K→E_{U_K}. The claim is that the following are equivalent:
(a) f_K extends to a section of U over S, i.e. it is an S-integral point.
(b) ψ comes from a section E_S→E_U.
(b') The composite E_K→E_{U_K}→E_U kills I_{x'}.

Grothendieck notes that (b)⇔(b') and (a)⇒(b) are clear, and that (b)⇒(a) is the real content.

Reduction steps:
- By descent (U is separated, so sections descend), reduce to S strictly local. Then E_K is its own inertia group and E_S = 1.
- Step by step along the elementary fibration tower ('de proche en proche'), reduce to U/S a smooth curve, U = X∖T. Here X/S is smooth and proper and T is a finite étale divisor of cusps (the letter T is overloaded).
- By the valuative criterion, f_K extends to a section f of X/S. What must be shown is f(S) ⊂ U, i.e. f does not meet any cusp at the closed point s.
- This is isolated as a Lemma for a smooth projective curve of genus g with ν cusps over a strictly local trait.

The next page proves the lemma by contradiction. If f meets cusp g_{i0} at s, then Y = Spec K → U induces H_1(Y,Z_ℓ) = Z_ℓ(1) → H_1(U,Z_ℓ). This map kills the part mapping to the Jacobian, since f is a regular point of X and hence of the Jacobian. So it lands in the toric part Z_ℓ(1)^I/Z_ℓ(1). There it equals m times the loop around the cusp, where m is the intersection multiplicity, so it is nonzero when ν ≥ 2. This contradicts (b'), where inertia must act trivially.

In modern terms: for a hyperbolic curve with good (log-smooth) reduction over a DVR, a rational point is integral iff its Galois section is unramified. It is a 'local, integral' compatibility of the section conjecture, stated more generally for elementary anabelian schemes.
errors: Notational overload: T denotes both the trait and the cusp divisor in U = X∖T; S and T are used interchangeably for the base.

The abelian (H_1) argument sketched for the lemma only works for ν ≥ 2. Grothendieck himself notes on the next page that the toric part vanishes when card I = 1. For g ≥ 1, ν = 1 one needs a non-abelian argument: the cuspidal inertia subgroup of π_1 of a hyperbolic curve is nontrivial, and the image of I_K is m-times a generator of it. On this page and the next this is left open.

The reduction from a general elementary relative scheme to the curve case ('de proche en proche') is asserted without detail. It requires the analogous statement for the homotopy exact sequences of each elementary fibration and is plausible but unchecked here.

The marginal hypothesis on the previous page (fibres 'élémentaires' of dim 1, not A^1 or G_m) leaves out the case (g,ν) = (0,2), G_m. That case is only partially covered later via the condition (g,ν) ≠ (0,1) and ν ≥ 2. For G_m the toric argument actually works, so the exclusion is over-cautious.

ideas.what: Integrality criterion: a K-rational point of a hyperbolic curve with good reduction over a DVR extends to an S-point iff its Galois section is unramified (kills inertia / descends to π_1(S)).
ideas.modern_name: unramified sections vs integral points; local behaviour of the section conjecture at places of good reduction
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in anabelian geometry; treated in work of Stix (thesis, 'Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups', LNM 2054) and others
ideas.where_published: possibly in J. Malgoire's transcription of La Longue Marche (Montpellier, 1995); not in Esquisse or the letter to Faltings in this form

ideas.what: Generalization of the criterion to 'elementary' relative schemes (towers of hyperbolic elementary fibrations) over a trait, with reduction to the curve case by induction.
ideas.modern_name: elementary anabelian schemes / Artin neighbourhoods; specialization of sections for good neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin (SGA 4 XI) for elementary fibrations; Grothendieck (Esquisse, letter to Faltings) for their anabelian role
ideas.where_published: anabelian role of elementary fibrations mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme / letter to Faltings 1983; this specific integrality statement unsure

ideas.what: Detection of meeting a cusp via the toric part of H_1(U,Z_ℓ) ≅ Z_ℓ(1)^I/Z_ℓ(1), after killing the Jacobian contribution because the rational section of the Jacobian is regular.
ideas.modern_name: weight/toric filtration of H_1 of an open curve; Kummer class of cusp

ideas.what: Reduction to strictly local base by descent; valuative criterion extending the point to X.
ideas.modern_name: étale descent of sections; valuative criterion of properness

missed.claim: The integrality criterion is formulated for higher-dimensional 'elementary' (anabelian) relative schemes over a trait, with a reduction to curves 'de proche en proche'. The higher-dimensional case of 'unramified section ⇔ integral point' for elementary anabelian schemes seems little treated in the literature, which focuses on curves.
missed.quote: On est ramené de proche en proche au cas où U/S est une courbe
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give a local integral compatibility for the section conjecture of higher-dimensional elementary anabelian varieties (Artin neighbourhoods), relevant to Stix/Schmidt–Hoshi-type results on anabelian good neighbourhoods.

missed.claim: The case of a single cusp (ν = 1, g ≥ 1) is left without proof, since the abelian H_1 argument gives nothing there. A non-abelian (cuspidal inertia) argument is needed.
missed.quote: NB cette partie est nulle si card I = 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. Today it is handled by injectivity of cuspidal inertia for hyperbolic curves, so it is a historical rather than open gap.

deep.surprise_reason: The page states and starts proving the 'integral point ⇔ unramified section' criterion, which is a precursor of later anabelian results on sections over DVRs. It frames this for elementary relative schemes in the 1981 Longue Marche notes. The curve case is essentially folklore now and the method is routine. The higher-dimensional elementary-fibration formulation is a mildly notable unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit $f_K$ / $K$ un pt de $U_K$ rat/K' should read 'Soit $f_K$ un pt de $U_K$ rat/K'. The stray 'K' is the subscript of f_K wrapping to the next line.
'{+37+}' is Grothendieck's own page number (37), not an insertion in the text.
'On est ramené de prouver ce cas[?] où U/S est une courbe' should read 'On est ramené de proche en proche au cas où U/S est une courbe'.
'Donc on est ramené finalement suivant[?] --' should read 'Donc on est ramené finalement au suivant --'.
'la conclusion p[?] que f(S) ⊂ U': the illegible word likely means '(la conclusion) signifie / est que'.
On the previous page, the marginal word read as 'ambitieux' is very likely 'anabélien' (U 'élémentaire' sur T, anabélien).
